answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit bids, with the stake slashable when independent audits prove fraud. Because one attacker cannot cheaply multiply identities without also multiplying locked capital, a sybil swarm raises the cost of entry in proportion to its apparent size; waiting for the horizon does not make the stake free. Auditors can sample transactions across the reef of markets, while jade-rated reputation helps route work only after honest performance, not merely after creating another account.
